domain.name: E-commerce & Digital Merchandising
domain.description: Practical catalog, merchandising, pricing, storefront, checkout, order, fulfillment, retention, and conversion operations for online commerce.

competencies.name: Product Catalog & Data Quality
competencies.description: Structure product titles, variants, attributes, media, inventory identifiers, and metadata.
competencies.purpose: Keep storefront and operations data consistent.

units.title: Catalog workflow
units.content: Define SKU and variant rules; normalize titles and attributes; attach accurate media; validate inventory and price fields; record source of truth; publish changes deliberately.

units.title: One product identity, many channels
units.content: Channel-specific copy can vary, but underlying SKU, variant, price, and inventory identity should remain consistent.

units.title: Catalog failures
units.content: Avoid duplicate SKUs, ambiguous variant naming, inconsistent units, missing dimensions, and channel edits that overwrite the source of truth.

drills.title: Audit a messy product catalog
drills.prompt: Find and prioritize catalog data defects.

competencies.name: Digital Merchandising & Collections
competencies.description: Organize collections, sort order, recommendations, bundles, and landing pages around shopper intent.
competencies.purpose: Make relevant products easier to discover.

units.title: Merchandising is guided discovery
units.content: Good merchandising reduces search effort by aligning assortment, grouping, messaging, and placement with real customer intent.

units.title: Collection workflow
units.content: Define audience and intent; select assortment; choose ranking logic; create supporting copy and media; review inventory; measure behavior; refresh stale placements.

units.title: Merchandising failures
units.content: Avoid burying high-intent items, promoting out-of-stock products, arbitrary collection logic, and optimizing clicks while ignoring conversion or returns.

drills.title: Design a collection page
drills.prompt: Plan a collection for a seasonal or use-case campaign.

competencies.name: Pricing & Promotion Operations
competencies.description: Manage base price, discounts, bundles, minimums, promo windows, and margin awareness.
competencies.purpose: Run promotions without accidental margin or trust damage.

units.title: Promotion workflow
units.content: Define objective; set eligible products and dates; calculate expected margin impact; define stackability; QA display and checkout; monitor results; end on schedule.

units.title: Discount depth is not the goal
units.content: A promotion should solve a specific objective such as conversion, inventory movement, or acquisition without unnecessary margin loss.

units.title: Promotion failures
units.content: Avoid hidden conditions, conflicting discounts, indefinite urgency claims, price display mismatches, and launch without checkout QA.

drills.title: QA a discount campaign
drills.prompt: Review a hypothetical promotion before launch.

competencies.name: Storefront UX & Product Detail Pages
competencies.description: Design navigation, search, PDP content, trust cues, mobile experience, and calls to action.
competencies.purpose: Reduce friction between product discovery and purchase.

units.title: PDP workflow
units.content: Lead with clear product identity and value; show essential media and specs; surface price, availability, shipping and returns context; answer common objections; keep the primary action obvious.

units.title: Mobile first means task first
units.content: Prioritize what a buyer must know and do on a small screen before decorative content.

units.title: Storefront failures
units.content: Avoid hidden shipping costs, image-only critical information, confusing variant selectors, weak accessibility, and CTA clutter.

drills.title: Review a product detail page
drills.prompt: Evaluate a hypothetical PDP for clarity and conversion friction.

competencies.name: Checkout & Payment Experience
competencies.description: Understand checkout steps, payment states, fraud signals, authorization, capture, failure recovery, and customer messaging.
competencies.purpose: Reduce preventable checkout abandonment while preserving controls.

units.title: Payment state matters
units.content: Authorization, capture, settlement, refund, chargeback, and failure are distinct operational states and should not be treated as interchangeable.

units.title: Checkout QA
units.content: Test cart, taxes, shipping, discounts, address validation, payment success and failure, confirmation, duplicate-submit behavior, and mobile flow using approved test methods.

units.title: Checkout failures
units.content: Avoid storing sensitive payment data outside approved processors, retry loops that duplicate charges, and exposing raw error details to customers.

drills.title: Build a checkout test matrix
drills.prompt: Create a non-production checkout QA matrix.

competencies.name: Order & Fulfillment Operations
competencies.description: Coordinate order states, picking, packing, shipping, exceptions, cancellations, and returns.
competencies.purpose: Keep customer promises aligned with operational reality.

units.title: Order lifecycle
units.content: Receive order; validate payment and inventory; release for fulfillment; pick and pack; confirm shipment; communicate tracking; handle exceptions; reconcile completion or return.

units.title: Exception ownership matters
units.content: Every stuck order needs a clear owner and next action, not just a status label.

units.title: Fulfillment failures
units.content: Avoid overselling, marking shipped before carrier handoff, losing exception reasons, and processing returns without matching the original order.

drills.title: Resolve a stuck order
drills.prompt: Work through an order with inventory and shipping exceptions.

competencies.name: E-commerce Conversion Analytics
competencies.description: Measure funnel behavior, product performance, abandonment, average order value, repeat purchase, and returns.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose where revenue is lost or improved.

units.title: Rates need denominators
units.content: Conversion metrics are meaningful only when population, event definition, time window, and exclusions are consistent.

units.title: Funnel analysis
units.content: Define stages; validate tracking; measure progression and drop-off; segment by device, source, or product; identify likely causes; test one change at a time.

units.title: Analytics failures
units.content: Avoid attributing every sales change to one campaign, mixing sessions and users, ignoring tracking gaps, and optimizing conversion while returns worsen.

drills.title: Diagnose a conversion drop
drills.prompt: Build a plan to investigate a sudden checkout conversion decline.

competencies.name: Retention, CRM & Lifecycle Commerce
competencies.description: Use post-purchase communication, segmentation, replenishment, loyalty, and win-back programs responsibly.
competencies.purpose: Increase repeat value without spam or manipulative tactics.

units.title: Lifecycle workflow
units.content: Map customer stages; define useful messages and triggers; segment on relevant behavior; set frequency limits; measure repeat purchase and unsubscribes; prune weak automations.

units.title: Value before frequency
units.content: More messages do not create retention if the content is irrelevant or mistimed.

units.title: Retention failures
units.content: Avoid dark-pattern consent, misleading urgency, excessive contact, and treating all customers as the same segment.

drills.title: Map a post-purchase journey
drills.prompt: Design a simple lifecycle flow for a repeat-purchase product.
